title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §119 of the post-'Longue Marche' notes, which studies the homomorphism from M (the profinite/étale fundamental group N_{1,1}^{ét} of the moduli stack of elliptic curves over Q, together with its subgroup M^!) to automorphism groups attached to the Fermat tower over P^1-{0,1,∞}. The previous page lists, for chosen data ρ,σ(,τ), groups of Ẑ-points of group schemes, keeping only sections compatible with components (the superscript Δ). Each is written as Ẑ* acting on a geometric factor: Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·L̂_0; G_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·𝔖^{+∧}; G^{⇆}_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·M^∧; N^~_ρ ≅ Ẑ*; N^{⇆}_σ ≅ Ẑ*·Ẑ; M~_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·(Ẑ×𝔖^{+∧}); M~^{⇆}_{ρ,σ} ≅ Ẑ*·(Ẑ×M̂). That page gives canonical maps M → M~_{ρ,σ} and M^! → M~^{⇆}_{ρ,σ}, which are to 'decompose into three'. This page carries that out.

(i) First, the composite M → γ^{ab}_{ρ,σ} = O*_{12}(Ẑ)^∧ ≅ Ẑ* is identified with 'the cyclotomic condition', i.e. the cyclotomic character, possibly written χ. Of the three components, M → N^~_ρ ≅ Ẑ* factors through π_Q^{ét} = Gal(Q̄/Q) and reduces to that condition. So it raises no interesting question.

(ii) Next comes the square (218): M → G_{ρ,σ} = Ẑ*·𝔖^{+∧} on top and M^! → G^{⇆}_{ρ,σ} = Ẑ*·M^∧ below. Here 𝔖^{+∧} and M^∧ are profinite completions of the oriented and unoriented (cartographic/modular-type) groups. Since the cyclotomic character (on M, or on M^!) is surjective, he asks whether these two homomorphisms are surjective.

(iii) Finally, M → N^{⇆}_σ factors through Galois as (219): π_Q^{ét} → N^{⇆}_σ = Ẑ*·Ẑ, a semidirect product ('1/2 direct'), i.e. an affine group Ẑ*⋉Ẑ. The image is a Kummer-type tower over the cyclotomic one. The question again is surjectivity.

He remarks that he can only hope to settle this 'by the arithmetic route': by proving that the map induced on π_Q itself is an epimorphism. The next page then sets up the Fermat curves X_n: x_0^n+x_1^n+x_∞^n=0. These are μ_n^{{0,1,∞}}/μ_n-torsors over U_{0,3} with S_3-action, forming the tower F_n → F_{n'} that realizes these groups concretely.
errors: No outright error, but the surjectivity questions are left open. For a Kummer-type map Gal(Q̄/Q) → Ẑ*⋉Ẑ, surjectivity can fail by a finite index because of entanglement between cyclotomic and Kummer extensions. The classic example is √2 ∈ Q(ζ_8), so the 2-power Kummer tower of 2 does not give a surjection. Whether (219) is onto therefore depends on which element or tangential datum σ defines the Ẑ-part. Surjectivity should not be presumed.

For (218), surjectivity onto Ẑ*·𝔖^{+∧} follows formally once the geometric part maps onto 𝔖^{+∧} and a rational splitting exists. The cyclotomic character is onto over Q, so the real content lies only in the geometric factor and in compatibility of the splitting. The page does not separate these issues.

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates explicit surjectivity questions for the maps from π_1^{ét}(M_{1,1}/Q) and M^! to the Ẑ*-extended oriented and unoriented cartographic groups acting on the Fermat tower. He also asks about Gal(Q̄/Q) → Ẑ*⋉Ẑ, and plans to attack these arithmetically. These are close in spirit to the Ihara–Anderson study of Galois on the metabelian/Fermat quotient, which came independently and later, but the specific formulation in his group-theoretic setup (ρ,σ data, Δ-sections) was never published.
missed.quote: on est amené à se demander si ces deux homs sont surjectifs ... notamment voir s'il est surjectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are of mild historical interest: they show Grothendieck independently turning to the Fermat tower as the abelian layer of anabelian Galois actions. Mathematically, the questions are largely subsumed by known results (cyclotomic surjectivity, Kummer entanglement, Ihara's Jacobi-sum power series).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a bookkeeping step that lists three components of a homomorphism and poses surjectivity questions. The only noteworthy element is Grothendieck's independent use of the Fermat tower in the Galois–Teichmüller context, which parallels Ihara–Anderson. There is no finished new result.
transcription_corrections: Equation numbers are (218) and (219), not (2.18)/(2.19); they continue the sequence (215)–(217), (220).
The target in (219) is N_σ^{⇆} (the superscript double-arrow used on the previous page, where N^{⇆}_σ ≅ Ẑ*·Ẑ), not N_σ^{Gal}.

The insertion above 'se réduit ici à' reads roughly 'à (via π_Q^{ét}) ladite condition'. The phrase is 'ladite condition', and π_Q^{ét} is a marginal insertion indicating that the map factors through Galois.
The isolated 'X.' at the start of the line after 'condition cyclotomique' is probably χ (the cyclotomic character) closing the previous sentence.

The last sentence likely reads 'Bien entendu, je n'ai de chances de le faire que par "voie arithmétique", en prouvant que l'homom induit sur π_Q lui-même est épi' ('prouvant', not 'presumant'; possibly 'chances' rather than 'doutes').
The underbrace label under γ^*_{ρ,σ} is likely O*_{12} (cf. O_N^* on the previous page), not 𝔖^*_{12}.
